result:
I'd hold the trial for now and wait for the operator's details-correct and cover/uncover report. The substitution is narrow enough to be safe, but the bytecode shows the image is never changed after it is handed to the screen. That makes "stale GPU copy" an unlikely cause, so a trial that fixes nothing would tell you very little.

## What I checked
- **`build/system-info-pane-complete.javap:219-227`**: `updateInfo` wraps the call in `SwingUtilities.invokeLater`. `setSystem` (164-217) calls `ArrayDrivePanel.updateInfo` with either the system or null. This matches your summary. I didn't redo the whole-JAR caller scan.
- **`build/lw-component-peer.javap:1812-1821`**: `createImage(int,int)` hands off to `LWGraphicsConfig.createAcceleratedImage`.
- **`build/cgl-graphics-config.javap:333-352`**: that call creates `new OffScreenImage(c, getColorModel(1), compatibleRaster, premult)`, which is software-backed.
- **`build/offscreen-image.javap`**: `initSurface` calls `clearRect` with the component's background (falling back to `SystemColor.window`). `createGraphics` uses the component's foreground and font, falling back to `windowText` and `Dialog 12`. It never touches acceleration priority.
- **One correction**: `java.awt.Image.accelerationPriority` defaults to **0.5**, not 1. That class isn't in the local dumps, so this comes from JDK source rather than this repo. Either way, any priority above 0 allows a cached GPU copy, so your premise still stands.

## Why a cached GPU copy is unlikely
In `build/drive-selection-complete.javap:1239-1704`, `syncDriveIcons` does this on every run, for each of the 14 drives:
1. Creates a **new** 18×68 image with `createImage` (line 1267).
2. Draws into it with `getGraphics` and `drawImage`/`tintIcon`. There is no `dispose`; I found none anywhere in the file, which matches the known disposal issue.
3. Passes it to `driveIcon[i].setIcon(new ImageIcon(img))` (1697-1701) and drops its own reference.

A cached GPU copy only goes stale when the same image is changed after it has been drawn to the screen. Here every refresh uses a new image object, so a cached copy of the old one can't appear under the new icon. Stale pixels fit better with one of these:
- the label or its area not being repainted, or a compositing problem;
- `syncDriveIcons` not running at all on the individual-drive-to-array path (each call I saw is behind a state check, e.g. 1880-1894);
- the state arrays it reads from being stale themselves.

## Why the operator report should come first
It costs nothing and splits the possible causes:
- **Cover/uncover fixes the icons**: the pixels are correct but weren't repainted, so this is a repaint or compositing problem. Only this branch makes the image trial worth running, and even here it's a weak candidate.
- **Cover/uncover leaves them stale, but details are correct**: the icon state wasn't recomputed. Look at the trigger paths for `syncDriveIcons` and the `driveStates`/`driveArrays` updates. The image trial is irrelevant here.
- **Details are stale too**: the data underneath is stale. The trial is irrelevant here as well.

## If you do run the trial: scope and side effects
- **Call site**: `DriveSelectionPanel` is constructed in several places (e.g. `build/help-prototype/model-consumers.javap:2352`, `4418`, `30444`, `50004`). Before anything else, record which one is the info view and which are wizard instances. Show that only that one call site's `new` and `<init>` owner changes, and that all others are identical bytecode.
- **Not displayable**: keep the "not displayable means null" behaviour. `Component.createImage` returns null when there's no peer. An override that always returns an image would quietly hide a crash the original would have hit after `removeNotify`, which changes behaviour beyond the trial.
- **Visual match**: `BufferedImage.createGraphics` doesn't take the component's colours or font. To match `OffScreenImage`:
  - fill with `getBackground()` (or `SystemColor.window`) when the image is created;
  - have `getGraphics` set the foreground and font the same way on every call, not just once at creation;
  - use the same fallbacks as above.
- **Pixel format**: `TYPE_INT_RGB` probably differs from `getColorModel(1)`. That's fine for opaque content and the existing SRC_OVER `tintIcon` blending, but say in the record that this is a deliberate difference.
- **Everything else**: the disposal issue, the shared renderer, polling and the EDT ordering stay unchanged, as you scoped. Performance impact is negligible (14 tiny images).

## Evidence to collect for the trial
- A bytecode diff limited to the new class plus that one call-site change, with the wizard call sites shown as identical.
- A runtime trace of the image's class and acceleration priority in the info view only, without native GUI or controller access, as with the earlier offline fixtures.
- An outcome rule written down before the run. A fix suggests image caching is involved but doesn't prove it. No change argues against caching, and only weakly, given the reasoning above.

**Recommendation:** get the report first, and run this trial only if cover/uncover clears the stale icons.
